summary: A brick tower on a heap of stone off Mobile Bay, built in 1873 on an island that eroded away around it; its keepers' house was swept off in the 1906 hurricane.

access.note: Town of Dauphin Island owns it; tower closed, offshore, visible from Fort Morgan.

corrections.why: The record's 1933 deactivation conflicts with the NRHP nomination and Lighthouse Friends, which show the light operating (automated 1947/48, dimmed 1966) until it was extinguished in 1971; the USLHS roster itself has keepers to 1947.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's differing first years are the three towers: 1838 (Lewis), 1859 (Leadbetter, 150 ft, built 1858), and 1873 (present). The NRHP statement line 'Constructed in 1875' contradicts its own text (1873).

notes_for_editor: Lighthouse Friends (secondary, copyrighted; paraphrased) supplies the 1830-1863 history, the 1925 dwelling, the 1916 hurricane commendations, Streckert's dismissal, George Hansen's drowning, Orsburne's 1947 ordeal and the 2001-2012 preservation steps; none was cross-checked in a primary source because the Light-House Board reports before 1891 are not in the corpus. Emma Hansen is named only by Lighthouse Friends. The Commissioner's estimates (1915) say October 1906 for the storm; two newspapers of 30 Sept and 3 Oct 1906 and USLHS give 27 September. The 1919 Bulletin names the tender in OCR garble (probably Camellia); the story leaves it unnamed. The NRHP form says the entrance was bricked up 'in 1906' and cites a 1975 interview with 'Tony Ryan (Last Keeper)'; the roster has Toney Ryan, but no source ties the two, so no link is made. The 1887 range lamp on the dwelling, the 1902 fog-bell tower move and the 1916 hurricane are in Lighthouse Friends only. Height: record has 38.1 m; NRHP gives 132 ft (40.2 m); USLHS tower_height_ft 125. The USLHS roster dates roles by span, not appointment. Keeper roster lines were taken as printed by roster.py (cite 1), not matched by table position by me. The 1932 Bulletin saving-of-life entry gives no event date. The 1924 rescue year is the Bulletin issue year; roster confirms Linton (first assistant 1924) and Ward (second assistant 1923-24). The 1966 beam change is from the NRHP only. The Propeller Club 2026 post is a local group's blog, used only for the present condition. The Commissioner's 1915 detailed estimates are printed in the volume of reports 1915-1922; citation uses printed page 87 (confirmed by the archive's scan data). Alabama Lighthouse Association/WKRG/Alabama News Center pages could not be read (blocked).
